items.title: Persist the reopen reason into the phase_transition audit event
items.context: buildPhaseTransitionProcessEvent (transition-orchestrator.ts) gains optional transitionType/reason appended only when defined; the call site passes { transitionType: 'reopen', reason: args.reason?.trim() } only when eventType === 'REOPEN'. Normal transitions must keep a byte-identical event shape so the flow-stability deepEqual shape test and all phase_transition consumers stay green. Reference: commit 05385c9.

happy.desc: A PLAN->INIT reopen with a valid reason appends a phase_transition event whose reason matches verbatim and whose transitionType is 'reopen', read back from the real persisted JSONL

edge.desc: A normal (non-REOPEN) transition produces a phase_transition event with neither transitionType nor reason, byte-identical to the pre-change shape

adversarial.desc: A reopen refused for a missing or too-short reason leaves the phase at PLAN and appends no event claiming a successful PLAN->INIT transition

verificationEvidence.note: Smoke drives a real CLI PLAN->INIT reopen from inside the worktree, then reads the PERSISTED process-events JSONL via StoryStore.readProcessEvents and asserts exactly one PLAN->INIT phase_transition event carrying transitionType=reopen plus the reason verbatim. One shared literal is now used both to send the reopen and to assert what was stored, so verbatim is a real round-trip rather than two literals that merely match. Verified RED: with the call-site fields removed the smoke fails on - the reopen phase_transition event must be marked transitionType=reopen.

Strict deepEqual pins the builder output for a normal REVIEW->TEST transition to the exact 8-key pre-change object, so neither transitionType nor reason appears when they are not passed. Reinforced end-to-end in plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke, which asserts the PERSISTED INIT_CHECK->PLAN event carries neither key using hasOwnProperty (key presence, so an explicit undefined would also fail). That end-to-end half matters because the builder-level deepEqual calls the builder directly and cannot see a call-site regression: verified RED by removing the eventType===REOPEN gate, which left flow-stability green but failed the persisted-event assertion.

A reopen with a MISSING reason is refused (non-zero exit, message cites the reason requirement), the phase is re-read as still PLAN, and the persisted JSONL is then asserted to contain ZERO PLAN->INIT phase_transition events at that point - checked after the refusals and before the real reopen, so any such event found would necessarily be spurious. Previously only the phase half was asserted. Honest scope limit: only the missing-reason branch is driven. A second refusal citing the same reason-requirement message reuses the same failure digest and trips the convergence breaker (gate-repeat 2>=2), which freezes the story and hard-blocks the legitimate reopen; observed directly while attempting to add a too-short case. The too-short branch shares the identical guard expression and error message.

items.title: Correct the overstated REOPEN checklist-reset atomicity comment
items.context: The reset (writeChecklist) and the phase write (writeStory) are two separate fs writes under a mkdir persist claim: concurrency-atomic and ordered so the phase write lands last, but not crash-transactional. Reword 'land together or not at all' to state the real guarantee and why the residual failure direction is the safe one. Comment-only. Reference: commit de46617.

happy.desc: The REOPEN checklist-reset comment states the real guarantee: concurrency-atomic via the mkdir persist claim, ordered so the phase write lands last

edge.desc: The phrase 'land together or not at all' no longer appears in that comment

adversarial.desc: The comment does not claim crash-transactionality anywhere, and explicitly names the residual crash window as the safe direction

verificationEvidence.note: Comment at transition-orchestrator.ts:896-923 now states the guarantee as CONCURRENCY-atomic via the mkdir persist claim, ORDERED so the phase writeStory runs LAST. Each clause independently verified against code, not taken from the reference commit: (1) mkdir-based claim - acquireMkdirLock (core/mkdir-lock.ts:253) acquires via mkdirSync(lockDir) at line 269 with EEXIST treated as held, so it is genuinely a mkdir lock; (2) ordering - grep shows acquire at line 859, reset write store.writeChecklist at 935, phase write store.writeStory at 937, release at 940, so the phase write is last inside the claim; (3) loser abort - the oldPhase re-read guard at lines 878-885 throws before line 935, so a losing concurrent writer never reaches the reset. npm --prefix packages/main run build exits 0.

verificationEvidence.command: grep -c "land together or not at all" packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts
verificationEvidence.note: Actual output: 0 (grep exit status 1, no match). The overstated phrase is gone from the file entirely, not just from this comment block. npm --prefix packages/main run build exits 0, confirming the comment-only edit did not affect compilation. git diff -U0 of my commit filtered for lines not starting with // returns nothing (exit 1), proving no non-comment line changed.

items.title: Clarify the scope of the dev_start worktree prune
items.context: pruneWorktreeRegistry (worktree.ts) runs `git worktree prune --expire now`, which cannot remove a live sibling worktree but does clear every currently-missing registration repo-wide, not just the calling story's. Document both facts so callers do not rely on it being story-scoped. Comment-only. Reference: commit 48b82c0.

happy.desc: The pruneWorktreeRegistry comment documents that git worktree prune --expire now cannot remove a live sibling worktree

edge.desc: The comment documents that --expire now is repo-wide over every currently-missing registration, not scoped to the calling story

adversarial.desc: The comment does not imply callers may rely on the prune touching only their own registration

verificationEvidence.note: grep prints line 578: "NOT the criterion. It therefore CANNOT remove a live sibling worktree: git leaves" - the comment block at lines 576-584 sits directly above pruneWorktreeRegistry and states the claim. Claim verified independently, not just read: on git 2.50.1 a scratch repo with main + 2 live linked worktrees + 2 missing ones was pruned via `git worktree prune --expire now -v` executed FROM linked worktree wt-live; output removed only worktrees/wt-goneA and worktrees/wt-goneB, and `git worktree list --porcelain` afterwards still showed wt-live and wt-live2 with their directories intact on disk. Live siblings are not prunable.

Comment lines 579-582 state: "`--expire now` is repo-wide, NOT story-scoped: one call clears the currently-missing registrations of every story, not just this one". Verified empirically on git 2.50.1: one prune invoked from worktree wt-live removed BOTH unrelated missing registrations (wt-goneA and wt-goneB), neither belonging to the caller - proving repo-wide, not caller-scoped. git docs agree ("run git worktree prune in the main or any linked worktree to clean up any stale administrative files"). I also CORRECTED the prior wording: the reference commit 5cb5914 claimed it clears EVERY currently-missing registration, which is false - a `git worktree lock`ed worktree survived two `--expire now` prunes with its directory deleted, so the comment now carries that caveat.

The comment explicitly forbids the reliance rather than merely omitting it: "callers must not rely on it to touch only their own entry" (line 582), preceded by "repo-wide, NOT story-scoped". It further blocks the opposite over-reliance (assuming the registry ends up fully clean) with the locked-worktree caveat at lines 583-584. Cross-checked the sole nearby call-site comment at line 996, which correctly attributes story-scoping to removeStaleWorktreeAdminDirs and says only that the prune leaves live siblings untouched - no contradictory story-scoped claim about the prune remains in the file. Diff is comment-only: the body `git("worktree prune --expire now", cwd)` is byte-identical, and `npm --prefix packages/main run build` (tsc) exited clean with no output.
